chapter: Raymond Scott, Kirby and postwar bands
title: Ben Webster in Kirby's band at the Aquarium
summary: Ben Webster makes up his own parts in Kirby's band, which has Ram Ramirez, Buster Bailey, Shavers and George Johnson, and Leeman and Hinton sort out the personnel.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Playing with Count Basie: the band, its feel and its people

blocks.x: So I went with the band, and they added Ben Webster, and Ben had done just the same thing with the arrangements that he did with Duke Ellington's band when he first joined him. He had no parts; he made his own. He made his own parts. Until they could write him some part. And you'd never know it, that's how people don't know the greatness of Ben Webster, how deeply he knew music, to sing with four saxophones and make a fifth part -- you don't do things like that.
Well, he did the same thing with John Kirby's band, and it was a fly book.
He was in that reorganized band -- Ben Webster?
Uh huh. And we had intended to take Billy Kyle's place, who was down in the South Pacific, and we got Ram. on piano -- Kirby got Ram Ramirez. He was a fine piano player.
Composer of 'Lover Man'.
Yes. And by the way, my first wife, Nita -- he was with Barnet for a while when we were in theatres, and he was stuck for ...
Beautiful.
That was on the way, that's just a side remark. George Johnson was a great saxophone player.
George James?
George Johnson.
George Johnson? I don't know George Johnson.
He was a very light-skinned boy, a great musician -- he was in the studios for awhile.
And you're sure it wasn't George James?
No, George Johnson -- and I think he just died this last year. I think. I don't like to say things like that unless I'm sure.
Sure ...

But I think he's among other friends that I lost along the way -- we added, or he added Ben Webster, played his own parts, and we went to work through thick and thin. Now we did that show -- I'm coming up with a scary one -- we did a 12 o'1 rehearsal into five o'clock and came off the air. And then I had a few hours to relax a little bit and go down from nine to four in the morning, or nine-thirty to four in the morning with John Kirby's band.
Yeah, who's was this show?
Now this is a double job, we're doubling now.
Yeah, but what was the show?
We had no show; well, I was on the CBS show.
Well, what did you do with John Kirby?
We played his book.
Where?
On the bandstand.
The bandstand in what club?
We went into the Aquarium.
Okay. The Aquarium. And can you tell me who the musicians were? John Kirby revised band -- not the O'Neal Spencer, not the Billy Kyle. Not the original band, this was the revised band.
Uh huh, yes.
And Cliff Leeman on drums, and Billy Kyle on piano?
No, Billy was in the army. Ramirez on piano.
Ram Ramirez, and there's John Kirby's the bass player and leader, and Buster Bailey -- was Buster Bailey there?
Right.
Is he?
Yes.
Okay, Buster Bailey is there. And Charlie Shavers ...
Charlie Shavers and Ben Webster, and George Johnson playing alto.
So we didn't have -- Russell Precape wasn't there?
No, he was in Georgia, in the army.
So you added a man, then. A tenor player.
Added a tenor man, and ...
It was a bigger band than the original John Kirby band.
One man more.
All right, okay. Thank you -- this is what I'm trying to find out.
